update.title: Built a seven-day sleep tracking dashboard
update.summary: Separated sleep presentation from collection, added on-demand multi-provider refresh, and produced day and week views for a tabbed desktop dashboard.

preview.description: Settings Hub Sleep page showing seven-day score, duration, and felt-quality trends

blocks.body:
## Give every consumer the same day and week views

Sleep Tracker owns reusable day and week view functions plus matching command-line operations. Human callers and the desktop dashboard receive the same structured payload instead of duplicating presentation rules.

The views combine watch-recorded sleep, diary ratings, manual corrections to bed and wake times, and environmental readings. Missing measurements remain gaps rather than becoming misleading zeroes.

blocks.label: Daily Check-In: the portable diary input

blocks.description: Sleep data flow from parallel provider refresh through typed collection and repository storage into day, week, and Settings Hub views. Refresh, collection, view formatting, and desktop rendering remain separate, observable stages.

blocks.body:
## Refresh independent providers together

Providers can declare an optional collection command and timeout. A refresh runs eligible sources in parallel and returns the result of each one, keeping an upstream failure distinct from a successful reading with no data.

The command line and API expose the same operation, so the dashboard can request fresh data through the tracker’s normal boundary.

blocks.description: Typed providers declare how to read a date and, when supported, how to refresh their upstream source before collection.

blocks.body:
## Render the week from declarative sources

Settings Hub defines the seven date tabs, trend view, dynamic labels, and polling behavior. Sleep Tracker owns date resolution, ratings, duration, score, and environmental summaries, keeping domain logic out of the desktop shell.

A custom 0–100 score combines sleep duration, time asleep relative to time in bed, sleep-stage balance, and the diary quality rating. The felt-quality trend shows the diary rating on its own.
